title: Basic 11 · Project a 3D structure
summary: Generate even Euler angles with VO EA, then project a β-gal volume at each angle with PJ 3Q to produce a projection stack.

steps.title: Try projection
steps.body:
To anchor the principle of cryo-EM analysis, practise the forward problem: **3D structure → 2D projection at a known viewing direction**.

Pipeline:
  1. Pull the **β-gal** map3d as a 3D structure.
  2. Generate an even Euler-angle set on the sphere with **VO EA**.
  3. Feed the volume + the angle set into **PJ 3Q (Project volume)** to get a stack of projections.

This is the "ground-truth" side of real data analysis (whose inverse is particles → angle estimation → 3D reconstruction) — a clean place to observe the principle.

steps.title: Drop the β-gal node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · β-gal**. A β-galactosidase map from the RELION tutorial.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.betagal` emits its default image (an average class).

steps.title: Click β-gal
steps.body: Click the β-gal node. The Inspector reveals `variant` / `class_index` / `size`.

steps.title: Set variant to map3d
steps.body: Change `variant` to **`map3d`** so β-gal emits its 3D density map; the right-hand output port switches to `volume`.

steps.title: Set size to 64
steps.body: Change `size` to **64**. A 64³ voxel grid keeps the compute fast (native is 128³); good for a lesson that finishes in seconds.

steps.title: Drop VO EA (Even Euler angles)
steps.body: From Reconstruction, drag **Even Euler angles** (`recon.voea`) — SPIDER's VO EA. It produces a (quasi-) uniform Euler-angle set on the sphere plus `eulers_csv` (phi,theta,psi text) and `num_angles`.

steps.title: Click VO EA
steps.body: Click VO EA. The Inspector reveals `delta_theta` (angular pitch), `theta_min/max`, `phi_min/max`, and `symmetry`.

steps.title: Set delta_theta to 30
steps.body: Enter **30** in `delta_theta` — theta pitch is 30°, phi is thinned proportionally to sin(theta). Result: roughly **~30 viewing directions** uniformly spread on the hemisphere (confirm in the `num_angles` output). Smaller values densify the grid (default 15° gives ~80).

steps.title: Drop PJ 3Q (Project volume)
steps.body: From Reconstruction, drag **Project volume** (`recon.pj3q`) — SPIDER's PJ 3Q. It projects a volume at the given Euler angles and returns the 2D projections as a stack.

steps.title: Wire β-gal.volume → PJ 3Q.volume
steps.body: Drag from β-gal's `volume` output to PJ 3Q's `volume` input — the 3D structure to project.

steps.title: Wire VO EA.eulers_csv → PJ 3Q.eulers_csv
steps.body:
Drag from VO EA's `eulers_csv` output (string port) to the ◇ (wireable marker) on PJ 3Q's `eulers_csv` parameter. Each row's viewing direction drives one projection.

With PJ 3Q's `batch` = ON (default), the output stack has one projection per row — `num_angles` frames in total.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body:
Press ▶ Run graph. β-gal map3d → VO EA builds the angle list; PJ 3Q projects the volume along each direction.

The PJ 3Q node shows a stack of projections. Sweep through them to see β-gal's shell + central hole from different viewing directions.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
**Play with it:**
  - Sweep VO EA's `delta_theta` 15 → 45 — the projection count rises/falls.
  - Set `symmetry` to `c2` / `d2` — restrict to the asymmetric unit, halving / quartering the angle count (β-gal is actually D2).
  - Toggle PJ 3Q's `method` between `fourier` and `real` — Fourier is ~20–50× faster at large box.
  - Turn `batch` OFF and set `phi/theta/psi` manually to get a single projection at a specific direction.

Reverse the flow (projection stack + angles → 3D) and you get the back-projection in **Comparison 3 · 3D reconstruction of β-gal**. Once projection is intuitive, that lesson becomes easy to follow.
